title: Dashboard lifecycle and trace-linkage notes
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight planning note that captures a proposed lifecycle for inference dashboards and a compact pattern for anchoring traces to dashboard widgets. The goal is to reduce dashboard sprawl, make drilldowns reliable for oncall, and ensure metrics have clear stewards and retirement criteria.

Audience
- Observability engineers
- SREs oncall rotation
- Serving/runtime/product engineers who own features

High-level lifecycle (proposed)
1) Draft stage (0-2 weeks): owner creates a single compact dashboard (operator view + two drilldown anchors). Mark status draft. Keep <= 6 primary panels.
2) Pilot stage (2-8 weeks): expose to canary owners. Add SLI definitions and associated trace anchors. Track query cost.
3) Active stage (8+ weeks): tag dashboard with steward, SLA, and retention. Dashboard accepted into daily oncall rotation if it passes: <2 slow queries, clear drilldown path, defined SLOs.
4) Review cadence (quarterly): every dashboard is reviewed for query cost and signal value. If not referenced in 6 months or has high query cost with low actionability, mark for pruning.
5) Retirement: archived with a deprecation note and retained minimal summary panels in a compact "legacy" dashboard for 90 days.

Metric stewardship and naming conventions
- Each metric must have a steward (owner). Stewards are responsible for instrumentation correctness, units and cardinality.
- Metric names: inference_<area>_<signal>_<unit> e.g. inference_runtime_latency_ms, inference_kv_cache_hit_ratio_pct
- Labels: service, model, deployment_tier (hosted|dedicated|private), region, tenant_id (hashed)
- Cardinality guardrails: tenant_id only on high-sample, low-cardinality aggregate metrics. If tenant_id pushed to high-cardinality metrics, route to trace sampling instead.

SLI mapping template (for each dashboard)
- User-facing latency SLI: 95th percentile tail on request path (prod, real-user)
- Availability SLI: Successful-response-rate over 10m window by model and region
- Quality SLI (optional): model regression alert tied to evaluation prompt-set failure rate
Include explicit definition, measurement query, alert threshold, and owner.

Trace anchoring patterns (compact, reproducible)
- Widget -> Trace mapping: every critical panel must include a small link button that opens a pre-populated trace query. Provide a compact set of trace filters: service=runtime, span.name~"generate|stream", model, request_id.
- Trace sampling: use severity-weighted sampling for tail latencies and error cases; light sampling for p95 and below.
- Session reconstruction key: (request_id, trace_id, kv_cache_key hash). Include these in logs to enable deterministic replay.
- Tokenized-inference specifics: annotate spans with token_count, kv_cache_warmth (cold|warm|partial), batch_size, and compile_variant. These tags enable fast grouping in the trace UI.

Drilldown anchors (recommended minimal set)
- Operator view (single page): KV cache heatmap, request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate. Each panel should link to:
  - Trace view anchored to selected time and model
  - Tenant-level breakdown (if applicable)
- Cost view: per-1000 token cost estimate (derived), GPU utilization by pool. Link to recent rollout changes affecting model size or quantization.
- Incident snapshot: a saved query that captures the last 5 minutes of critical spans and recent config changes (deploy hash, routing rules).

Query performance guardrails
- Any dashboard panel should aim to finish < 1s for oncall default time range (1h). If a panel is slower, provide a lower-fidelity cached panel for oncall and move heavy queries to a separate "analysis" dashboard.
- Avoid unbounded wildcard joins in the dashboard backend. Pre-aggregate where possible (minute buckets, model-level aggregates).

KV cache / cold-cache investigation checklist
- Is kv_cache_warmth present on spans? If not, add immediately.
- Compare tenant-level hit_ratio against global hit_ratio (5m window).
- Correlate cold-cache spikes with: deployment events, model variant rollouts, traffic shifts, or database eviction logs.
- If warmth unknown, fallback to using prefix-match of request prompt length vs cached prefix length as heuristic.

Oncall checks and playbook snippets (short)
- When p95 latency spikes: check operator view -> open trace anchor -> filter by span.duration > p95 and group by compile_variant and batch_size.
- When error rate rises: open incident snapshot -> correlate deploy hash -> roll back or route to smaller model variant.
- Cost regression: check per-1000-token cost panel and recent quantization changes.

Dashboard pruning and audit process
- Monthly: list dashboards created in last 12 months and last-viewed timestamps.
- Quarterly: steward signs off on retention or deprecation. If no sign-off, auto-tag for archive.
- Archive policy: archived dashboards kept for 90 days in read-only form, then deleted unless reinstated.

Instrumentation checklist for new signals
- Semantic contract: human-readable definition, units, intended cardinality, and example queries.
- Schema test: automated test that asserts metric emits in staging with expected labels.
- Cost estimate: approximate query cost (tokens/rows scanned) during 1h window.
- Trace linkage: ensure at least one span annotation or log field maps to metric labels for deterministic drilldowns.

Open questions / discussion items
- How aggressive should auto-archival be for dashboards owned by small feature teams?
- Should tenant_id be hashed at the ingestion layer or closer to storage to reduce risk?
- What is the acceptable upper bound on query latency for oncall use (1s is a suggestion)?

Next steps / action items
- (Ava) Draft a dashboard review checklist and circulate to SRE and serving runtime teams by 2024-12-10.
- (Marco) Prototype the trace-anchor link button in the dashboard UI (POC) and file a PR: github:repo/ops-dashboards#34.
- (Priya) Run a cost audit for top 20 dashboards by query cost and report by 2025-01-07.

Appendix: example PromQL-like queries (illustrative)
- p95 latency by model: quantile_over_time(0.95, histogram_quantile_bucket_sum(inference_runtime_latency_ms_bucket{job="runtime"}, 5m))
- kv cache hit ratio: sum(rate(inference_kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))

Notes on uniqueness
This doc is intentionally compact and operational: it combines lifecycle governance with concrete trace-linkage patterns and guardrails for low-latency oncall flow. It is meant to be a pragmatic complement to longer-term observability strategy docs.
